answer: The main difference between the current evaluation paradigm and a mechanistic understanding of AI risks is that the current paradigm is heavily situated within risk management frameworks, such as Responsible Scaling Policies (RSPs), which only seek to detect when AI capabilities pass arbitrary capability thresholds. In contrast, a mechanistic understanding of AI risks involves a deeper comprehension of the underlying mechanisms and interactions that contribute to those risks, rather than merely identifying when certain thresholds are crossed.
